Privacy policy

  • App: Bukin Mic Recorder
  • Developer: bukin
  • Contact: dev.mechanics998877@gmail.com
  • Effective date: 2026-10-11

This policy explains what the app does with your information. The app is a microphone recorder that saves uncompressed WAV files. It works with USB and built-in microphones. It is not a phone-call recorder.

Summary

  • The app records audio only when you start a recording or a Mic Test.
  • Recordings are saved as WAV files in the place you choose: the app's own storage on your device, or a folder you pick.
  • The app has no internet permission, no ads, no analytics and no accounts. It does not send your recordings or other information to the developer or to anyone else.
  • Recordings can still leave your device through things outside the app's control, such as a cloud folder you chose or files you copy or share yourself.

Microphone

The app asks for the microphone permission. It uses the microphone only:

  • While you record. Audio from the microphone is written to a WAV file.
  • During a Mic Test. The app reads audio to show a live level meter. Mic Test audio is processed in memory and is not saved to a file. The test stops when you leave its screen.
  • Briefly when a recording or Mic Test starts, to find a recording format your microphone and phone support.

The app never starts recording on its own.

Recording in the background

When you start a recording, it keeps running if you switch to another app or turn the screen off. While it runs, Android shows an ongoing notification with a Stop button, and the recording continues until you stop it, an error occurs (for example, the microphone is disconnected or storage is full), or Android ends the app.

On Android 13 and later the app also asks for permission to show notifications, so that the recording notification can appear. If notifications are turned off, the app warns you before recording. Recording still runs normally in the background, but the notification and its Stop button are not shown in the notification shade. You can still stop the recording in the app.

Where recordings are stored

You choose where recordings are saved:

  • App storage (default). Files are saved in the app's own folder on your device's shared storage (Android/data/bukin.wavrecorder/files). Android deletes this folder when you uninstall the app, so copy any recordings you want to keep before uninstalling. On Android 10 and earlier, other apps with storage permission may be able to read files in this folder.
  • A folder you pick. If you choose a folder with Android's folder picker, recordings are saved there. That folder may belong to another app or service, such as a cloud storage app. That service may copy, sync or back up your recordings under its own terms and privacy policy. Files in a picked folder are not deleted when you uninstall this app.

The app does not encrypt WAV files. They are protected by Android's normal storage protections and by the folder or service you chose.

How long recordings are kept, and deleting them

Recordings are kept until you delete them. You can delete recordings individually or in bulk in the app's Library. You can also delete them with a file manager or in the folder you picked. A file that is still being recorded or repaired cannot be deleted from the Library until it is finished.

Crash recovery and other app data

To protect a recording if the app or phone stops unexpectedly, the app keeps a small private record of the file it is currently writing: the file's name and location, and its recording format. After an interruption, the app uses this record to repair the file so the audio already captured can be played. The record is removed once the file is finished or repaired.

The app also stores, privately on your device:

  • your chosen file-splitting interval;
  • the folder you picked, if any;
  • a short note about how the last recording ended, so the app can tell you after it restarts.

This information stays on your device. The app may also write technical diagnostic messages to Android's system log on your device, such as file names, the microphone's name and the recording format. The app does not send these messages anywhere.

Backups and moving to a new phone

Android can back up app data to your Google account and copy it to a new phone. For this app, Android's backup and device-transfer features include only the file-splitting interval. They exclude recordings, the folder you picked, crash-recovery records and other device-specific data.

These rules apply only to Android's own backup and transfer features. They do not control separate backup, sync or file-transfer tools, including a cloud storage app that holds a folder you picked.

Information shared with the developer or third parties

The app has no internet permission and contains no advertising, analytics, tracking or crash-reporting code. The app itself does not collect, sell or share your personal information or recordings.

If you install the app from Google Play, Google provides the developer with statistics such as install counts and, if you agreed to share usage and diagnostics data with Google, crash and performance reports about the app. Google processes this data under its own privacy policy.

Children

The app is intended for a general audience and is not specifically designed for children.

Visiting this policy webpage

This privacy-policy webpage is hosted on GitHub Pages. GitHub logs visitor IP addresses for security purposes. This is separate from the app, which does not upload recordings or include analytics. See the GitHub Privacy Statement.
